**About The Company**
CrowdStrike is a global leader in cybersecurity, protecting the people, processes, and technologies that power modern organizations. Since 2011, the company’s mission has been to stop breaches and help customers stay secure in an increasingly connected world. Its AI-native Falcon platform supports security operations across industries, helping organizations protect their businesses, communities, and customers.
  
  
CrowdStrike operates large-scale distributed systems that process nearly three trillion events each day, with data volumes continuing to grow. The company is committed to innovation, customer focus, and responsible AI adoption. Team members are encouraged to work with flexibility and autonomy while using AI thoughtfully to accelerate execution, develop expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex challenges.
  
  
**About The Role**
Join a team focused on making customers’ security-relevant data continuously available for automated detection and response, threat hunting, and other Falcon use cases. This role contributes to the systems and services that help security teams access timely, reliable data and act on potential threats. Working in a high-scale environment, you will partner with colleagues across engineering and product teams to improve the availability, performance, and resilience of data-driven security capabilities.
  
  
The work calls for curiosity, sound technical judgment, and a strong sense of ownership. You will help address complex challenges involving distributed systems and evolving data demands, while keeping customer needs at the center of technical decisions. You will also contribute to a culture of responsible experimentation and continuous learning, including the thoughtful use of AI where it can improve the quality and efficiency of your work.
  
  
**Qualifications**
Successful candidates bring experience building, operating, or improving software systems, with an interest in reliable services and data-intensive workloads. You should be comfortable investigating technical problems, understanding trade-offs, and communicating your reasoning to teammates. Experience with distributed systems, data processing, cloud-based services, or security products can be valuable, as can familiarity with software development practices such as code review, testing, monitoring, and iterative delivery.
  
  
We value candidates who approach challenges with a customer-focused mindset, collaborate across disciplines, and take responsibility for the quality of their work. Clear communication, adaptability, and a commitment to learning are important. You should be open to using AI tools responsibly, evaluating their outputs carefully, and applying them in ways that support sound engineering practices.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Contribute to the design, development, and ongoing improvement of services that make security-relevant data available to Falcon capabilities. Help build systems that can support high volumes of events while meeting expectations for reliability, performance, and operational readiness. Investigate issues, identify root causes, and work with teammates to deliver practical, durable solutions.
  
  
Collaborate with engineering, product, and other partners to understand requirements and translate them into effective technical approaches. Participate in design discussions, testing, code reviews, and service operations. Monitor system behavior, share findings, and help identify opportunities to improve scalability and resilience. Apply responsible AI practices to support research, development, and problem-solving while protecting the quality and integrity of outcomes.
  
  
**Benefits**
CrowdStrike offers an environment centered on meaningful work, flexibility, and professional growth. Team members have the opportunity to contribute to a mission with real-world impact, collaborate with colleagues across a global organization, and work on challenging technology at significant scale. The company encourages autonomy, continuous learning, responsible AI adoption, and innovation. Specific compensation, benefits, and work arrangements may vary by position and location.

CrowdStrike is committed to building an inclusive workplace where talented people can contribute and grow. Employment decisions are made in accordance with applicable laws and without discrimination based on protected characteristics. We welcome applicants with varied experiences and perspectives who share a commitment to customers, colleagues, and the mission to stop breaches.

**Description**
Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.
  
  
**What You'll Work On**

* Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
* Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
* Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
* RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
* System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.

Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.
  
  
**What You'll Work On**

* Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
* Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
* Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
* RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
* System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.

**Our Stack**
Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. Automated hardware-in-the-loop testing and rich fleet telemetry let you see the impact of your code in the real world. New development is increasingly in Rust.

**About the Company**

Surgeon Decision Intelligence (SDI) develops AI-driven medical imaging solutions for orthopedic care. Founded by orthopedic spine surgeons and medical students from the Hospital for Special Surgery, the company focuses on developing quantitative imaging biomarkers to inform treatment decisions and predict outcomes for musculoskeletal diseases.

SDI combines computer vision, medical image analysis, and machine learning to extract insights from MRI scans and help translate research into clinical practice. The team works closely with surgeons, clinical collaborators, and research partners to develop accurate, interpretable, and reproducible solutions.

**About the Role**

Surgeon Decision Intelligence is seeking a Software Engineer, Data & ML Infrastructure to build and maintain the data systems and infrastructure supporting its AI/ML platform. Working directly with the Senior AI/ML Engineer, you will develop and maintain the PostgreSQL clinical and imaging database, cloud storage for medical imaging studies, internal APIs, and the tooling and CI/CD infrastructure that supports reliable machine learning development.

This is a hands-on software engineering position rather than a research role. You will write production-quality Python, manage database migrations, develop data validation tools, modernize legacy research code, and build internal services used by machine learning and clinical teams. The role offers the opportunity to work with medical imaging and applied machine learning in a regulated healthcare environment.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop and maintain the PostgreSQL database layer, including schema changes, SQLAlchemy ORM models, Alembic migrations, and data-integrity constraints.
* Build and maintain data ingestion, validation, and ETL pipelines for clinical outcomes data and medical imaging metadata, including DICOM.
* Contribute to internal FastAPI services and develop endpoints for imaging metadata, annotations, and access control.
* Support Azure cloud infrastructure, including blob storage for imaging studies, containerized service deployments, and authentication and authorization workflows.
* Migrate legacy research code into versioned, dependency-managed Python packages that follow established engineering standards.
* Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines, automated tests, and developer tools to improve code reliability and reproducibility.
* Build tools that support machine learning workflows, including dataset extraction and export, experiment and artifact tracking, and data provenance.
* Participate in code reviews and contribute to engineering standards, technical documentation, and collaborative development practices.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* At least 3 years of professional software development experience using Python.
* Solid knowledge of SQL and relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including schema design and query optimization.
* Experience with software development lifecycle practices, including version control, testing, CI/CD, and collaborative development workflows.

About Discernis

Discernis builds AI for legal discovery at a scale where general legal AI tools fall apart. When a litigation team needs to know what a group of people knew, and when, across millions of emails, chats, and documents, our platform finds it with the recall attorneys can stake a case on. We deploy in private cloud and fully air-gapped on-prem for AmLaw firms and corporate legal teams.

We're seed-stage and venture-funded, have paying Big Law customers, and have a pipeline of AmLaw firms and Fortune 500 companies lined up for paid pilots and future deals. Industry incumbents are coming to us to integrate. Discovery is our wedge: the bigger goal is helping enterprises understand and act on their largest, messiest datasets. We're a small team based in NYC, and you'd be joining before our next stage of growth.

How we work

We value ownership, curiosity, and shipping. We hire people who teach themselves new things, make good calls without much direction, and care about getting it right for the attorneys who depend on us. We work hard at a sustainable pace, without crunch culture or arbitrary deadlines.

The role

Today our founder runs the AI stack personally. He holds a Columbia PhD in AI and built Amazon's first customer-facing RLHF pipeline. You'll take the stack over, all of it: agentic workflows, retrieval and evaluation, inference optimization, fine-tuning, and post-training. For your first ~90 days you'll work side by side with him. After that, you set our AI direction and grow the team around it.

At a larger company, this would be three separate roles. Here, it's one. This is likely the single highest-impact role at the company, and we need someone who can do the engineering and the science.

Rough split

* **~40% agentic systems:**
  orchestration, tool use, and reliability
* **~20% inference:**
  serving and optimization, including small models on constrained on-prem hardware
* **~40% longer-horizon research:**
  model adaptation, post-training, and RL

Problems you'll own

* High-recall retrieval and synthesis across billion-token document collections
* Agents that are reliable, testable, and deployable, not just impressive in a demo
* Getting strong performance from small open-source models in air-gapped environments
* Evals that capture what "correct" means to a litigator
* RL that trades off tool use against compute

Our stack

* **Models:**
  open-weight models we fine-tune, adapt, and post-train for legal reasoning, then serve as our own versions
* **Serving:**
  vLLM on our own H100 and H200 GPUs
* **Deployment:**
  the same models run in private cloud and fully air-gapped customer environments
* **Language:**
  Python
* **Around it:**
  PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes (K3s), Vue

What we're looking for

* You've trained or post-trained real models (fine-tuning, RLHF, or RL). Experience calling APIs is not enough.
* You've also shipped LLM or agentic systems to production that real users depend on.
* You have strong evaluation instincts and know how to tell real gains from noise.
* You have hands-on inference and serving experience.
* **When you apply, please include a link to a repo, paper, write-up, or system you built.**

We're hiring for this role across levels, from strong AI engineer to AI lead. Compensation reflects the level we hire at.

Nice to have

* Experience on a big tech AI team or at an AI startup
* A PhD or MS in ML
* Research publications or open-source work in LLMs, agents, RL, or evaluation
* Distributed training or large-scale GPU experimentation

Our process

1. A call with our founder
2. A screen with our Head of Engineering
3. A deep dive on a real problem

Why Discernis

* Research problems with a direct path to production and paying customers
* A founder who speaks your language
* Meaningful equity with a 4-year vest and 1-year cliff
* Health insurance
* Unlimited PTO plus standard US holidays

If you need an accommodation during the hiring process, email us at admin@discernis.ai.

**About Us**
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
  
  
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
  
  
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
  
  
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
  
  
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
  
  
****The Job****
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
  
  
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
  
  
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
  
  
**About You**

* You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
* You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
* You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
* You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
* You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
* You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
* You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
* You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.

****Nice to have:****

* Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
* Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
* Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
* Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

****What we offer:****

* Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
* Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
* Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
* Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
* Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

*https://www.mintmcp.com/hiring/mcp*

* Cloud & AI Infrastructure (AWS): Deploy, monitor, and scale resilient infrastructure on AWS—including per-tenant KMS encryption, CI-enforced PHI routing, AWS Bedrock integrations, and our upcoming self-hosted GPU inference pipelines for proprietary clinical speech and language models.

What We Are Looking For

* Full-Stack Mastery: Strong production experience with React (modern hooks, state management, complex interactive UIs like calendars and data grids) and Node.js (REST/streaming APIs, asynchronous job queues, webhook processing), ideally in TypeScript.
* Deep Relational SQL Skills: Proven ability to model complex relational data, optimize slow queries, manage migrations safely, and implement database-level security (such as Row-Level Security / RLS) where data isolation is non-negotiable.

* AWS Cloud Proficiency: Practical experience building and deploying on AWS (e.g., ECS/EKS, Lambda, RDS, S3, KMS, IAM, CloudWatch, or Bedrock) with a strong grasp of security best practices.
* High Ownership & Product Empathy: You care deeply about user experience. Our standard is that an agency office manager should be productive in their first hour without a manual. You write clean, maintainable code and can take a feature from a rough problem statement all the way to production.

Bonus Points (Nice to Have)

* Experience with healthcare compliance and standards (HIPAA, PIPEDA/Quebec Law 25, BAA boundaries, EVV, or X12 EDI transactions like 837P/835/270/271).
* Experience with self-hosted AI/ML inference (NVIDIA GPUs, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, vLLM, or Whisper/ASR pipelines).
* Experience building native bilingual (English/French) applications where localization follows the individual user across UI, emails, SMS, and generated PDFs.
* Prior experience integrating Stripe, Plaid, Twilio, Aircall, or payroll APIs (QuickBooks, Gusto, ADP, Paychex).

Why Join Tunzly?

* High-Impact Architecture: No legacy bloat or micro-management. You will shape core architectural decisions across our full-stack web platform, mobile caregiver experience, and proprietary AI engine.
* Real-World Meaning: Every workflow you automate and every millisecond you shave off the interface gives nurses, coordinators, and caregivers more time to focus on patient care rather than paperwork.

Compensation: Competitive base salary, meaningful early-stage equity, flexible remote-first work culture, and modern hardware/tooling of your choice.

**About Oath Technologies**
Oath Technologies is a new research organization building tools for oversight of advanced AIs. As AIs become more powerful, it will become more difficult to understand and monitor their behavior. Oath is building oversight tools based on formal verification: rather than monitor AIs directly, humans define unambiguous rules, and AIs must provide trustworthy mathematical evidence of compliance. In this way, Oath will help keep humans safe and in control as AI advances.
  
  
Oath is a Focused Research Organization (FRO) incubated and fiscally sponsored by Convergent Research. Convergent has incubated 12 FROs spanning mathematics, astrophysics, neuroscience, climate, biology, and AI, including the Lean FRO (formal mathematics and verification) and E11 Bio (whole-brain circuit mapping). Oath is led by CEO Dr. Mike Dodds, and is based in Berkeley, CA.
  
  
**Role Summary**
Oath's research engineers will build novel formal methods tools and apply them at scale to AI oversight problems. To do this, we are hiring both formal methods specialists and engineers with skills such as developer tools, scalable testing, agent development, AI/ML, and others that complement Oath's mission. Engineers may have skills in one or several areas, and our team will be tightly integrated, with both categories working together.
  
  
Oath will target very difficult verification and oversight problems, far beyond previous formal verification projects in scale and complexity. Oath's research team will work iteratively, building tools, testing them on our flagship problems, identifying failures, and then feeding those back into our tool designs.
  
  
We plan to build an Oath team of around six people by the end of year one, growing to a steady state of around twelve people by year three. Oath's roadmap runs for five years, and we’ll set more ambitious targets as the outcomes of our work and changes in the profile of AI risk evolve. This is a strong fit for people who want to tackle complex, high-stakes challenges in a nimble, collaborative organization.
  
  
Oath's current plan is to build tools across three families: \*\*design\*\* (authoring new specifications), \*\*lifting\*\* (extracting specifications from existing systems that have none), and \*\*audit\*\* (stress-testing specifications for gaps or adversarial manipulation). We're applying these to a first flagship target, verified agent containment: proving that an AI agent can't escape the permissions and sandboxing meant to bound it, from the OCI container runtime down to Linux kernel isolation primitives. Most of this work will be done in Lean or adjacent formal-verification infrastructure, with AI agents doing much of the day-to-day drafting and proving under close review.
  
  
**Primary Responsibilities**
